The shaft is solid, circular, and prismatic with diameter d = 30 mm and total length L = 1200 mm, modeled in N–mm–MPa units.
The shaft is fixed (clamped) at x = 0 and free at x = 1200 mm.
The material is AISI 1020 steel with shear modulus G = 76,923.1 MPa.
The only applied loads are torsional: T1 = +200,000 N·mm at x = 1200 mm and T2 = −200,000 N·mm at x = 400 mm.
There is no transverse shear force, bending moment, or axial load; "shear loading" refers only to the torsional shear stress.
Small-deformation, linear-elastic behavior is assumed, and warping/rigid-body out-of-plane effects are neglected (pure torsion of a circular shaft).
The polar moment of inertia is J = πd⁴/32 = π(30)⁴/32 ≈ 79,521.6 mm⁴.
Global moment equilibrium about the shaft axis gives the reaction torque at the fixed end as T_R = −(T1 + T2) = 0.
Internal torque in segment 400–1200 mm (found by sectioning from the free end) is constant at T = +200,000 N·mm.
Internal torque in segment 0–400 mm is constant at T = T1 + T2 = 0 N·mm, since the two applied torques balance outboard of this segment.
Note: the internal torque magnitudes in the two segments are NOT equal; only the outboard segment carries torque, so the reaction torque is zero and only the 400–1200 mm segment twists.
Maximum torsional shear stress in each segment is computed as τ_max = T·c/J with c = d/2 = 15 mm.
For segment 400–1200 mm: τ_max = 200,000(15)/79,521.6 ≈ 37.7 MPa; for segment 0–400 mm: τ_max = 0.
The maximum shear stress occurs at the outer surface of the loaded segment and is well within typical yield limits for AISI 1020 steel, consistent with linear-elastic assumptions.
The angle of twist at x = L relative to the fixed end is φ = Σ(T_i·L_i)/(J·G) over the segments.
Segment 0–400 mm contributes zero twist because its internal torque is zero.
Segment 400–1200 mm contributes φ2 = (200,000 × 800)/(79,521.6 × 76,923.1) ≈ 0.02615 rad ≈ 1.50°.
The total angle of twist at the free end is φ_L ≈ 0.02615 rad (≈ 1.50°), in the positive (T1) sense.
Reported response quantities: internal torque diagram per segment, maximum torsional shear stress per segment, reaction torque at the support, and total angle of twist at the free end.
